repos.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
repos.paper_summary:
OpenGCUA is the first release of an ongoing project to open the full stack for generalist computer-use agents (GCUAs), which choose at each step what to observe, how to act, and how to organize work across GUI, accessibility-tree, shell, and API interfaces. The release includes the implementation, prompts, trajectories from eight frontier models, and preliminary real-device harness and cross-device SDK. It does not include a newly trained model.

The paper studies two mechanisms. Code execution has the model write one Python program per step that combines PyAutoGUI calls, `bash()` shell commands, and control flow, so intermediate results can determine later operations without another model call. Harness-to-model decision transfer lets the model decide when to request screenshots and how to track task state.

On the offline OSWorld-v2 set, the full configuration raises mean partial score by 19.6 points across all eight models and cuts steps per task by 53.0% relative to batched GUI-only execution. Against a GUI+CLI baseline, code execution adds 6.1 points and cuts steps by 14.8%. On four real macOS tasks, Qwen3.8-Max uses 19.4 times as many reasoning tokens as GPT-6 Astra. The authors state that the harness and SDK remain preliminary.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Open Generalist computer-use agent project releases agent designs, evaluation trajectories and preliminary tools, without a trained model.

digest_headlines.heading: Generalist CUA: Definition and Positioning
digest_headlines.headline: A generalist computer-use agent is defined by three per-step decisions: what to observe, how to act, and how to organize work.

digest_headlines.heading: Agent Design: Code Execution and Harness-to-Model Decision Transfer
digest_headlines.headline: Code execution and model-requested screenshots are tested on OSWorld-v2 with gains in task score and cache reuse for selected models.

digest_headlines.heading: Real-Device Generalist CUA
digest_headlines.headline: On four real macOS tasks, Qwen3.8-Max averages 50.2K reasoning tokens per task against 2.6K for GPT-6 Astra under one harness.

digest_headlines.heading: Roadmap
digest_headlines.headline: The next release is planned to add a trained generalist computer-use model, with work on efficient reasoning and real-device benchmarks.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Existing open computer-use models focus on graphical interfaces, while hybrid graphical-and-programmatic systems are only beginning to appear.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Across eight models, the full configuration raises mean partial score by 19.6 points on the offline OSWorld-v2 subset.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists evaluation details, real-device task descriptions, the prompts, and trajectory examples from GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.

repos.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
repos.paper_summary:
MemT-1.0 is a family of memory foundation models that keep history inside the model's computation rather than in an external context window or retrieval store. The released models are MemT-1.0-Nano (36B parameters, 3B activated, 10M dynamic memory) and MemT-1.0-Flash (288B parameters, 17B activated, 336M dynamic memory). It builds on the earlier Metis model, replacing token selection with a token-level update based on Gated DeltaNet-2 and adding Mixture-of-Storage to scale memory capacity. Training is continued pre-training followed by post-training on 34B tokens.

Across 11 memory benchmarks, the models outperform parametric memory baselines on average and remain competitive with retrieval-augmented methods, while largely preserving general capabilities under the noise setting. At a 128K-token history, Nano reaches about 1.86× end-to-end inference speedup and a 66× reduction in persistent storage relative to a full-context KV cache. On SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual, internalized experience improves average task success over agents without experience.

The memory state is fixed-size, so its capacity is bounded and precise recall may degrade as history grows.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: MemT-1.0 upgrades the Metis memory design and releases 36B and 288B parameter models with Mixture-of-Storage.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Architecture
digest_headlines.headline: Native memory runs as a parallel attention branch in selected Transformer blocks, with backbone layers left unchanged.

digest_headlines.heading: Training
digest_headlines.headline: Backbone preparation and a two-stage pipeline train memory by distilling from a frozen full-context teacher on 34B tokens.

digest_headlines.heading: System and Infrastructure
digest_headlines.headline: Windowed execution of Mixture-of-Storage cuts peak memory by 80.1% for a 32K-token pack, adding 1.6% to forward-backward time.

digest_headlines.heading: Memory Scaling Behavior
digest_headlines.headline: Memory score rises from 36.65 to 46.80 over two post-training epochs, and four experts beat two by up to 2.69 points.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Native memory averages 50.6 on memory benchmarks for Flash and 47.0 for Nano, ahead of parametric baselines but behind textual systems.

digest_headlines.heading: Application in Agentic Tasks
digest_headlines.headline: Stored procedural experience raises the coding benchmark success rate from 66.07% to 69.33% without experience text in context.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations and Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: A fixed-size memory state limits recall of detail, and the relation between local and hyper memory remains unresolved.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: MemT-1.0 outperforms the evaluated parametric baselines on average, preserves general capabilities under noise, and points to future memory scaling.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix gives author lists, memory configurations, projection and gate initialization, training settings, and a stability bound for the update.

repos.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
repos.paper_summary: Hy-Nomas is an 8B-parameter video world model that generates interactive video from free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple turns. It is built on HunyuanVideo 1.5 and generates variable-length segments conditioned on the current input and cached history. Its main design choice is action-aware causal attention: structured captions describe persistent scene and subject context that stays visible to later segments, while timestamped action instructions are limited to their own time window. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer converts user requests and interaction history into structured conditions for each next segment. Training follows a multi-stage curriculum (causal generation, text interaction, camera control, training on model-generated histories), then diffusion distillation. Human evaluation is reported as favoring Hy-Nomas over existing world models, but the text provided does not include the scores. The paper notes that temporal causality does not establish physical causality, that robotics adaptation is shown only as an initial LoRA demonstration, and that retrieving past views does not update off-screen state, such as a clock that should keep running. Weights, code, and benchmarks are released.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Hy-Nomas is an 8B interactive world model that follows free-form text and camera commands across multiple turns.

digest_headlines.heading: Data
digest_headlines.headline: Training videos are filtered, deduplicated, and annotated with camera trajectories and structured captions.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Architecture
digest_headlines.headline: Action-aware causal attention limits each action to its own time window, and camera tokens condition each segment.

digest_headlines.heading: Training Infrastructure
digest_headlines.headline: Sequence parallelism, compute-balanced packing and masked attention kernels support training on sequences up to 360K tokens.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Training
digest_headlines.headline: Training proceeds through causal, interaction and context curricula, then distillation from 100 to 4 steps per segment.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Inference
digest_headlines.headline: A vision-language Prompt Enhancer turns user requests into segment captions, and inference is optimized for a single device.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Human raters prefer Hy-Nomas over three interactive world models on most tasks, but Genie 3 leads on spatial memory.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Hy-Nomas is placed among video-based world models that add text and camera control to diffusion video generators.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion and Future Directions
digest_headlines.headline: Discussion names open challenges: response latency, action-grounded robotics, retrieval-based memory, and detailed caption quality.

digest_headlines.heading: Contributors
digest_headlines.headline: Contributors section lists core contributors, contributors, acknowledgments and leadership acknowledgments.

repos.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
repos.paper_summary: Scaling in Games (Zhang, Chen, Yang et al.) is a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) for embodied game agents that vary data volume, data diversity, and model size. The authors train 120 configurations spanning 0.8B to 27B parameters, 50 to 1,600 hours of gameplay, and five mixtures from Minecraft-only to multi-game. Models take screen frames and output keyboard-mouse actions. Evaluation covers in-corpus worlds (Minecraft, Doom), related worlds (OmniGameArena), and distant worlds (GameWorld), using validation losses and benchmark scores. Diversity improves related-world transfer, while distant-world gains stay limited. Larger models use data more efficiently but generalize worse under single-game training. A three-factor scaling law fits training, Minecraft, and in-corpus losses with R² of 0.980, 0.982, and 0.995. On MCU, the 27B-S1 model reaches 63.3% average success, and under real-time evaluation the 9B-S3 model scores 25.3 versus 19.2 for the best frontier model tested. The limits are that training is behavior cloning without task feedback, and the distant-world gap persists.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Virtual worlds vary in visuals, physics, controls and goals, so the study asks whether heterogeneous gameplay data helps or interferes.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Earlier virtual-agent work used single-environment specialists or foundation models, and none isolated data, diversity and model size together.

digest_headlines.heading: Preliminaries and Experiment Framework
digest_headlines.headline: The study frames gameplay as reason-then-act steps and trains a 120-configuration grid over model size, data budget and mixture.

digest_headlines.heading: Scaling and Generalization in Heterogeneous Virtual Worlds
digest_headlines.headline: More data and diversity improve in-corpus and related-world results, but gains in distant worlds stay limited.

digest_headlines.heading: Comparing with Frontier Models
digest_headlines.headline: Models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds and lead frontier models in real-time play.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion and Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Gains in related worlds do not reliably reach distant worlds, and the imitation objective may help explain the gap.

digest_headlines.heading: Ethics Statement
digest_headlines.headline: Training uses publicly released gameplay datasets under their licenses, and the authors collect no new recordings or personal data.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers mixture accounting, the out-of-distribution validation set, sparse reasoning annotations and comparisons with related scaling studies.

repos.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
repos.paper_summary: This technical report evaluates GPT-6-Astra, a model whose weights stay fixed, on 12 embodied benchmarks covering tabletop manipulation, dexterous hands, humanoids, household tasks, and navigation. Under a unified protocol, the model gets a frozen knowledge package built from each benchmark's training demonstrations, and episodes run with either the standard step limit or up to 10× that limit. At the standard budget, it matches or exceeds the best published result on most settings, with the largest margins on LIBERO-Ultra-Long and DexJoCo. Reported success rates are 81.9% on RoboDojo and 87.3% on DexJoCo. On SIMPLE, task-level ICL raises success on four common tasks from 70.8% to 90.8%. In a RoboDojo harness ablation pairing the model with a π0.5 controller, closed-loop review plus ICL reaches 54.17% success, versus 15.56% for the baseline. Limitations include weaker transfer when test tasks differ from the training data, high token and time cost, and failures in physical verification, irreversible errors, and long-horizon progress.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: The report asks what a general model's embodied competence implies, and where the field should go next.

digest_headlines.heading: Large-Scale Study under A Unified Protocol
digest_headlines.headline: At the standard budget, the model matches or exceeds the best published result on most of twelve settings.

digest_headlines.heading: Harness Ablation
digest_headlines.headline: Closed-loop review improves success by up to 20.00 percentage points over open-loop execution, at higher token cost.

digest_headlines.heading: Real-World Validation
digest_headlines.headline: Zero-shot control succeeded in 17/18 rigid pick-and-place trials but 0/11 plug insertion trials.

digest_headlines.heading: Towards a Next-Generation Embodied Benchmark
digest_headlines.headline: Current benchmarks were designed for imitation-trained policies, so the report proposes three principles for next-generation designs.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: GPT-6-Astra is a clear advance in embodied capability, but benchmark success does not yet imply reliable deployment.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists contributors, related work, empirical studies of frontier models, and per-platform real-world results.

repos.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
repos.paper_summary:
Latent Sparse Attention (LSA) is a sparse attention layer for ultra-long context. It clusters keys in a learned latent space, and each query scores cluster centroids instead of every key. Keys are pooled four to one, grouped into buckets by Ward's agglomerative clustering, and queries pick top buckets (flat search) or descend a tree with beam search (Tree, which is subquadratic in prefill). Attention then runs over sink, window, and selected keys. Distilled-LSA (D-LSA) adds LSA to a frozen pre-trained model by training only small per-layer projections and a temperature against the frozen layer's attention. Native-LSA (N-LSA) is trained on next-token loss alone.

Evaluation uses RULER and PaperTrail, a long-context scientific reading benchmark the authors built. At 10M tokens, one D-LSA attention layer prefills 22.7× and decodes 4.6× faster than sparse attention on GLM-5.3-Flash, and 72.4× and 42.5× faster than full attention on Qwen-3.8-27B, with similar accuracy. N-LSA matches full-attention accuracy with a 1.6× per-layer training speedup at 128k tokens.

Limitations: the KV cache still grows linearly with context, tree search loses accuracy faster than flat search past 1M tokens on GLM-5.3-Flash, and N-LSA was tested only at about 0.5B parameters with flat search.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Sparse attention indexers that score every key dominate cost at ultra-long context, so LSA clusters keys instead.

digest_headlines.heading: Sparse Attention
digest_headlines.headline: At 10M tokens the indexer takes 98% of sparse attention's prefill time, and current indexers still scan every key.

digest_headlines.heading: Latent Sparse Attention (LSA)
digest_headlines.headline: LSA clusters keys in a learned latent space, and each query scores only bucket centroids, flat or as a tree.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: D-LSA keeps accuracy close to baselines up to 10M tokens, and N-LSA matches full-attention validation loss at 128k.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: Tree search loses accuracy faster than flat past 1M tokens, and native training was tested only at small scale.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: LSA offers a practical route to ultra-long context attention, through distillation of pre-trained models or native training.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers oracle key-budget tests, method symbols, training data, PaperTrail, evaluation setup, and parallelism details.

repos.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
repos.paper_summary: HiP3R is a hierarchical pose-graph method for globally consistent camera trajectories and 3D geometry from long video, applied on top of existing feed-forward backends without retraining. A coarse stage optimizes a chunk-level Sim(3) graph with overlap edges and progressively scheduled loop edges, using confidence-weighted IRLS alignment on a bounded number of point correspondences. A fine stage holds that layout fixed and estimates one shared SE(3) camera per frame, with relative-motion factors within chunks and placement priors from every overlapping chunk. On seven benchmarks, with VGGT-Omega, mean ATE falls from 18.555 m to 4.906 m and mean RPEtrans from 0.9878 m to 0.0622 m. With LingBot-MAP, mean ATE falls from 8.288 m to 4.017 m. On KITTI, VBR, and Oxford, HiP3R reaches a mean ATE of 11.25 m versus 17.71 m for VGGT-Long with loops. On ETH3D, Neural RGB-D, and 7-Scenes, Chamfer drops from 0.0759 m to 0.0272 m. The paper notes that compact indoor sequences leave little room for correction, and lists robustness to unreliable loop closures and online updates as open directions.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Long videos processed in overlapping chunks yield inconsistent frame poses that chunk-level alignment alone cannot fix.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior long-video methods use chunk-level alignment or streaming memory, and this work adds global loops and per-frame consistency as post-processing.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: A two-stage pose graph first fits chunk similarities with loop closures, then optimizes one shared camera per frame.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Across seven benchmarks, HiP3R reduces macro trajectory error from 18.555 to 4.906 m with VGGT-Omega and from 8.288 to 4.017 m with LingBot-MAP.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: HiP3R improves trajectory and surface accuracy on indoor and outdoor benchmarks, while online updates and unreliable loop closures remain open.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix covers Jacobian derivations, keyframe subgraph rules, solver settings, dataset splits, runtimes, and ablations on loop noise and placement.

repos.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
repos.paper_summary: OpenVLHarness is a multimodal tool-use harness for MLLMs, built around a capability layer and persistent multimodal memory. The capability layer wraps heterogeneous perception, search, and computation tools behind task-level interfaces and renders their outputs into model-readable observations. Memory registers images, structured data, and web references under handles, and a Python Coding Agent runs generated programs over stored values, so later steps can reuse earlier evidence. The harness is evaluated on 22 benchmarks across four domains with eight backbones. Averaged over the 22 datasets, it raises Qwen3-VL-8B from 34.2 to 45.4 and Qwen3-VL-32B from 38.3 to 50.9, outperforming OctoTools and Visual Sketchpad. With GPT-6 Luna at medium effort, it scores 56.5 against 45.8 for the base model, and it is reported to outperform Codex and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort while using at most 37% of their model-token cost. Qwen3-VL results are means of three seeds; GPT-6 results are single runs, so their variance is unreported in the main table. The paper's benchmark-level gains are uneven, with some datasets, such as V* for Qwen3-VL-8B, showing no gain.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Extra reasoning budget gives diminishing returns, so the paper proposes OpenVLHarness to add multimodal evidence acquisition.

digest_headlines.heading: Harness Design
digest_headlines.headline: OpenVLHarness pairs a capability layer that renders tool outputs with persistent memory of handle-addressed artifacts.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: OpenVLHarness raises Qwen3-VL-8B scores on 22 benchmarks, for example from 32.00 to 48.56 on a counting benchmark.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior visual tool-use systems use fixed plans or task-specific frameworks, while this paper keeps multimodal artifacts addressable across turns.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Released harness gives broad gains on 22 benchmarks and can specialize to domains without updating model weights.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix reports tool-call volume, capability distribution, paired accuracy effects, and object-count distributions of benchmarks.

repos.title: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
repos.paper_summary: The Agentic Scientist is a scaffold that runs coding agents through a computational research campaign, from task specification to manuscript. A drafting pipeline turns a research brief into an initial program, evaluators, and a task contract. Parallel workers run research cycles in which an ideation agent writes a structured hypothesis with target rubrics and an execution agent tests it within a fixed budget. Workers share distilled memory at cycle boundaries. The selected program then gets controlled baselines, ablations, and post-hoc analysis, and a writer agent drafts a LaTeX paper that an audit agent checks against the results. A meta-trained evolution strategy matches or exceeds CMA-ES on 5 of 7 unseen Brax tasks. An Error Diffusion paper produced with the system was accepted at ALIFE 2026. Across 70 campaigns, higher search scores predict higher AI reviewer scores on 4 of 5 tasks. The autoillustrate figure tool scores 37.5 against 25.0 for PaperBanana on PaperBananaBench. Limitations: the metric is an AI-reviewer proxy, only one paper had external review, task drafting is unreliable for larger tasks, and evaluation covers only computational machine learning.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: The paper introduces The Agentic Scientist, a scaffold that lets human researchers run end-to-end computational research with coding agents.

digest_headlines.heading: Background & Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Existing AI scientist systems cover parts of the research loop, but lack a reusable orchestration and evidence layer.

digest_headlines.heading: The Agentic Scientist: An Orchestration Layer for Research Agents
digest_headlines.headline: The scaffold runs task drafting, parallel investigation with contracted cycles, retrospective ablations, and grounded paper writing with audit.

digest_headlines.heading: AI Co-Scientist and Conference Paper Submission
digest_headlines.headline: A single paper written with the system was accepted at ALIFE 2026 after human verification and manual edits.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluating The Agentic Scientist Across Tasks, Harnesses, and LLMs
digest_headlines.headline: Across 70 campaigns, final task performance was positively associated with AI reviewer scores on four of five tasks.

digest_headlines.heading: Additional Case Studies: Putting The Agentic Scientist to work
digest_headlines.headline: Search raised multi-needle retrieval accuracy to 98.0% and reinforcement-learning fine-tuning validation accuracy to about 71.9%, with evolution-strategy results mixed.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluating autoillustrate on PaperBananaBench
digest_headlines.headline: autoillustrate scored 37.5 overall against 25.0 for the best PaperBanana variant, below the human reference of 50.0.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Coding agents can contribute to research in an orchestrated workflow, but unstated specifications, proxy metrics and narrow domains limit the evidence.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers related work, per-task discoveries, CMA-ES and Error Diffusion results, experimental protocols, and figure examples.

repos.title: Sequent-Prover: Training Agents for Formal, Checkable SMT-based Reasoning
repos.paper_summary: Sequent-Prover is a family of language-model agents and the post-training recipe that produces them. The agents write SMT-LIB programs, run them in Z3 across several turns, read the solver feedback, and then give a final answer. The recipe, verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation, samples teacher rollouts and keeps correct traces that are executable, non-trivial, and grounded in the input as Gold. It trains by supervised fine-tuning on Gold traces, then by DPO, using weaker or failed traces as negatives. The evaluation covers 37 benchmarks with 7,254 problems per model family and four samples per problem. For the 4B model, per-attempt accuracy rises from 85.6% to 97.0%, and pass^4 rises from 0.641 to 0.917. Average SMT calls fall from 4.10 to 2.52. For the 27B model, the base pass^4 is already 0.977, and DPO reaches 0.986. The paper states that a solver cannot check whether a formalization matches the intended problem. Its grounding and non-triviality measures are proxies for that check.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Solver access alone does not ensure reliable reasoning, so the paper trains models to build grounded SMT-LIB formalizations across multi-turn Z3 use.

digest_headlines.heading: Methodology
digest_headlines.headline: Verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation keeps only correct, grounded, executable solver traces and trains on them with supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization.

digest_headlines.heading: Results
digest_headlines.headline: Post-training raises the 4B model's average per-attempt accuracy from 0.856 to 0.970 and pass^4 from 0.641 to 0.917.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Works
digest_headlines.headline: Prior work in theorem proving, solver synthesis, tool feedback and reinforcement learning motivates the SMT-LIB target and solver-native repair.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Solver use can be learned as a formal-reasoning policy that turns sample-dependent successes into stable, grounded and refutational behavior.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: A solver can check a formal artifact but cannot confirm the abstraction is the intended one, so semantic faithfulness stays unverified.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists Z3 proof modes, the agent loop, datasets, training details, teacher accuracy, and worked solver trajectories.
